label: Jānu siers
note: Eaten at Jāņi, the midsummer festival; under 30 % fat; a firm cylinder, not a spreadable cooked cheese

about.text: Jāņu siers is a Latvian sour milk cheese eaten at the Jāņi midsummer festival. Its curd comes from both soured and fresh cow milk and is cooked with eggs, butter, salt and caraway into a firm cylinder. It has been an EU Traditional Speciality Guaranteed since 2015.

how.label: cook curd with egg, butter, caraway
how.text: Whole milk is heated and curd added; the mass is cooked until curds separate from clear whey, then stirred with egg, butter, salt and caraway into a firm ball. The temperature and size figures come from Wikipedia, not from the TSG regulation.

steps.note: Lactic acid bacteria only, no rennet; no species named.
Cooked until the curds separate from the clear whey, which is drawn off at 72-77 °C.

steps.name: mix
steps.note: Stirred with egg, butter or cream, salt and caraway seeds into a firm ball.

steps.name: rest
steps.note: In cheesecloth, often pressed, for a few days in a cool place.

processing.text: Lactic acid bacteria only, no rennet; no species named. The soured-milk curd is then cooked.
